# Judge brief: q1-memory-system

## Shared context and measured evidence

Ecosystem: Claude Code (Opus 5.5) and Codex CLI (GPT-6 Astra) need ONE shared, local-first long-term memory: automatic capture of sessions, query over MCP or hooks, project scoping, recovery. North star: US-equities research and native agent engineering. User constraints: upstream official artifacts rather than self-builds, passwordless and low-friction operation, evidence plus convergence as the source of truth. Hosts: a 64 GB M5 Pro Mac as the control machine, plus an RTX 4090 WSL2 workstation for evaluations.

Neutral measurements (our harness, the official LongMemEval-S cleaned retrieval protocol, recall_all@5 over sessions, 470 questions, full track, each system as shipped):
- agentmemory 0.9.29 with MiniLM: 0.821
- dense retrieval with Qwen3-Embedding-4B: 0.753
- BM25: 0.747
- ai-memory 2.5-pre (the current production system) with MiniLM: 0.496
- ai-memory with FTS only: 0.400

ai-memory with its production Qwen3-4B embedder is still finishing. A preregistered rule requires +5 pp and significance to replace production. Caveat: agentmemory was fed through its REST remember API, not its shipped hook path.

---

# Return A

**As of 25 September 2026, I would benchmark these five in order.** This ranks suitability for your harness and deployment. All scores below are vendor/maintainer reports; I found no independent reproduction matching your exact local configuration. Adapter descriptions are engineering proposals, not tested integrations.

1. **Hindsight — strongest complete shared-memory candidate.** [MIT repository](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight); latest [v0.10.1, September 21](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight/releases/tag/v0.10.1), including Codex transcript/timestamp fixes. Documented [Claude Code/Codex hooks and MCP](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/sdks/integrations/coding-agents) provide automatic capture. Supports [Ollama/OpenAI-compatible inference](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/developer/configuration); operational weight is API/worker plus [PostgreSQL and vector extension](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/developer/installation).

   **Evidence:** [December 14, 2025 paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.12818v1): LongMemEval-S **91.4% QA**, LoCoMo **89.61%**, Gemini-3 Pro answers, GPT-OSS-120B memory/judge. Current [manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vectorize-io/agent-memory-benchmark/main/results-manifest.json) reports **94.6%/92.01%** respectively and BEAM-10M single-query **64.08%**; exact run date/model are missing.

   **Adapter/risk:** [Retain](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/developer/api/retain) timestamped sessions as separate documents; aggregate [ranked facts’ document IDs](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/developer/api/recall) into sessions. Extraction cost and accuracy with your smaller local models remain unmeasured.

2. **Attemory — strongest directly relevant reported retrieval result; conditional on dependency verification.** [MIT repository](https://github.com/AttemorySystem/attemory); latest [v0.1.3, August 13](https://github.com/AttemorySystem/attemory/releases), evidencing continuing releases.

   **Evidence:** Undated [benchmark files](https://github.com/AttemorySystem/attemory/blob/main/benchmarks/LongMemEval.md), checked today: **96.38% session recall_all@5**, cleaned LongMemEval-S/470, local Qwen3.5-9B; **83.62%** on M. These are retrieval scores, without an answer model. [LoCoMo QA](https://github.com/AttemorySystem/attemory): **94.52%**, GPT-4.1-mini answers/GPT-4o-mini judge; run date missing.

   **Adapter/risk:** Reuse dated-turn ingestion and session deduplication; match assistant-turn inclusion across controls. [Runtime](https://github.com/AttemorySystem/attemory/blob/main/doc/usage.md) requires its own local Qwen/GGUF service and KV storage, outside your Ollama/OpenAI endpoint convention. Claude integration covers code search; MCP remains planned and automatic dual-client capture is unverified. The required [prebuilt core SDK](https://github.com/AttemorySystem/attemory/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt) leaves full source/licence coverage unverified.

3. **GBrain — auditable retrieval challenger with native client support.** [MIT repository](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain); latest [v0.56.2.0, September 24](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/releases/tag/v0.56.2.0), with active indexing/sync fixes.

   **Evidence:** [September 6 evaluation](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain-evals/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/2026-09-06-longmemeval-ranker-wave.md), v0.48.4.0: cleaned S, **449/470 = 95.53% all-session coverage within five chunks**. Uses OpenAI text-embedding-3-large and Voyage rerank-2.5; five chunks differ from five distinct sessions. Separate **86.6% QA** uses Sonnet 4.6/GPT-4o judging. Equivalent local scores are missing.

   **Adapter/risk:** [Ollama providers](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/integrations/embedding-providers.md), Bun and embedded PGLite support local deployment. [Claude/Codex MCP and capture](https://github.com/garrytan/gbrain/blob/master/docs/guides/bootstrap.md) require bootstrap; Codex capture is SessionEnd-only. Preserve timestamps/session IDs, over-fetch chunks and deduplicate in returned order. Use one shared server owner. Published results depend on hosted models; the latest release also acknowledges an unresolved macOS reindex hang.

4. **Mem0 OSS — useful extraction-plus-hybrid baseline.** [Apache-2.0 repository](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0); latest Python [v2.2.0, September 23](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/releases), following September 18 updates.

   **Evidence:** Undated [OSS results](https://github.com/mem0ai/memory-benchmarks): LongMemEval-S **91.0% QA**, GPT-5 extraction/answer/judge, Qwen-600M embeddings. Published **94.4% LongMemEval, 92.5% LoCoMo**, and BEAM-1M/10M average scores **0.641/0.486** belong to the managed platform.

   **Adapter/risk:** [Ollama](https://docs.mem0.ai/components/llms/models/ollama) is supported; benchmark infrastructure uses API plus Qdrant. Native capture plugins target the cloud ([Claude](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/issues/7105), [Codex](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/main/docs/integrations/codex.mdx)); local capture needs glue. Use fresh collections, source-session metadata and session aggregation. Encode dates in text/metadata because [OSS rejects native timestamp parameters](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0/blob/main/mem0/memory/main.py). Cloud/OSS feature and score differences are material.

5. **OpenViking — integration-focused comparison.** [AGPL-3.0 repository](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking); latest [v0.4.21, September 20](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/releases), following September 14. Offers native [Claude](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/agent-integrations/02-claude-code)/[Codex](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/agent-integrations/04-codex) hooks+MCP, [Ollama/OpenAI-compatible providers](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/guides/01-configuration), and a server with embedded storage.

   **Evidence:** [May 29 report](https://blog.openviking.ai/post/openviking-benchmark-results/), v0.3.22: LoCoMo **80.32% QA with Claude Code**, Doubao 2.0 Pro VLM; separately identified answer model missing. A [LongMemEval harness](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/tree/main/benchmark/longmemeval/openviking) exists, but no verified published score was located.

   **Adapter/risk:** Ingest timestamped sessions; maintain URI→session provenance and aggregate [ranked URI hits](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/07-retrieval). Risks are AGPL requirements, provenance through extraction, and Codex hook/version restrictions.

For all five, use the [official evaluator](https://github.com/xiaowu0162/LongMemEval/blob/main/src/retrieval/run_retrieval.py): fresh stores, gold labels excluded from ingestion, identical role inclusion, and five distinct returned sessions. Measure ingestion cost and latency alongside recall. No verified MemoryAgentBench results were located for these five.

---

# Return B

## Verdict (2026-09-25)

None of the systems below publishes recall_all@5. MemPalace and agentmemory publish recall_any over 500 questions. QA figures are vendor-run with varying answer and judge models. Vendor QA leaders (90–95%, unverified): Hindsight, Mem0, Honcho and Zep. Published-retrieval leaders: verbatim hybrids. V = vendor-reported.

I re-scored MemPalace's committed per-question logs ([raw](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/develop/benchmarks/results_mempal_raw_session_20260414_1629.jsonl), [hybrid](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/develop/benchmarks/results_mempal_hybrid_v4_held_out_session_20260414_1634.jsonl)) with your metric:

- Raw MiniLM over **user-turns-only** session text: recall_all@5 **0.857** on 470 questions.
- Hybrid v4 without an LLM: **0.887** on the 424 held-out non-abstention questions.

Both beat agentmemory's 0.821. If your BM25 and Qwen3 baselines index whole sessions, re-index user turns first.

## Ranked shortlist

1. **MemPalace**: cheapest to run, likely beats 0.821. [repo](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace), MIT, v3.10.0 (2026-09-16).
   - V, April 2026 ([bench](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/blob/develop/benchmarks/BENCHMARKS.md)): LongMemEval-S cleaned recall_any@5 96.6% raw, 98.4% hybrid on held-out questions, no LLM.
   - Raw mode bypasses the palace code; palace modes score 89.4% and 84.2% ([#214](https://github.com/MemPalace/mempalace/issues/214); [critique](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.21284), 2026-04).
   - Local ChromaDB with ONNX embeddings, no services. Hook plugins for Claude Code and Codex, plus MCP.
2. **Hindsight**: strongest vendor claims, MIT, local models, hooks for both agents. [repo](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight), MIT, v0.10.1 (2026-09-21).
   - V; reproduced by Virginia Tech collaborators. LongMemEval-S QA, 500 questions: 91.4% with Gemini-3, 83.6% with gpt-oss-20b ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12818), 2025-12).
   - BEAM-10M 64.1% ([blog](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/blog/2026/04/02/beam-sota), 2026-04). [Live page](https://benchmarks.hindsight.vectorize.io/) shows 94.6% on AMB, where Gemini answers and judges. Retrieval recall is not published.
   - Local LLMs through Ollama or llama.cpp. One plugin shares a bank between Claude Code and Codex. Embedded Postgres; an LLM extracts facts on every retain.
3. **QMD**: local reranking control you already run. [repo](https://github.com/tobi/qmd), MIT, v2.8.3 (2026-08-16).
   - Published results: none found.
   - BM25 plus local GGUF embeddinggemma, Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B and query expansion. MCP and a Claude Code plugin, but no session-capture hooks. SQLite only.
4. **Mem0 OSS**: new hybrid retrieval; measure the platform-to-OSS gap. [repo](https://github.com/mem0ai/mem0), Apache-2.0, v2.2.0 (2026-09-23).
   - V ([bench](https://github.com/mem0ai/memory-benchmarks)): platform LongMemEval 94.4% (answer model unstated), LoCoMo 92.5%.
   - Open source: 88.6% with Gemma 4 31B extraction, GPT-5 answering and judging. The README says some optimizations are platform-only.
   - Competitor re-run: 73.8% with GPT-5 answering ([Maximem](https://www.maximem.ai/blog/state-of-ai-memory-2026-claimed-vs-observed), 2026-05-27).
   - Ollama config, embedded Qdrant; the Claude Code plugin needs a Platform key ([docs](https://docs.mem0.ai/integrations/claude-code)).
5. **Honcho**: sessions are first-class, with hybrid message search. [repo](https://github.com/plastic-labs/honcho), AGPL-3.0, v3.2.1 (2026-09-24).
   - V ([blog](https://plasticlabs.ai/blog/research/Benchmarking-Honcho), 2025-12-19): LongMemEval-S 90.4% (Haiku 4.5 answering, GPT-4o judging), BEAM-10M 0.406.
   - Claude Code plugin, Codex hooks, MCP.
   - Needs Postgres, Redis and a deriver worker. Cloud models by default; local via OpenAI-compatible endpoints, though the embedder can silently fall back to OpenAI ([#915](https://github.com/plastic-labs/honcho/issues/915)).

## Adapters

- **MemPalace**: run `longmemeval_bench.py` raw and hybrid-v4 (no LLM rerank), scoring recall_all from `ranked_items`. Also test the production path: mine dated transcripts, then query MCP search.
- **Hindsight**: one bank per question. Call `retain(transcript, timestamp, document_id=session_id)`, then `recall(query_timestamp=question_date)`. Rank sessions by first-seen `document_id`.
- **QMD**: write `<qid>/<session_id>.md` with the date in front matter, one collection per question. Run `qmd query --json -n 50` and compare runs with the reranker off.
- **Mem0**: add turn pairs with `metadata.session_id`, which the vendor harness omits. Rank sessions by their best `search(limit=200)` hit.
- **Honcho**: one workspace per question, one Honcho session per haystack session. Rank sessions by `session_id` in workspace search results.

## Not shortlisted

- **Graphiti/Zep**: [repo](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti), Apache-2.0, v0.30.2 (2026-09-08).
  - LongMemEval-S 71.2% with gpt-4o, V ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13956), 2025-01).
  - 90.2% with gpt-5.4, product unstated ([research](https://www.getzep.com/research/), 2026-08).
  - Needs Neo4j or FalkorDB and LLM extraction per episode.
  - Adapter: one episode per session; map edges to episodes.
- **Supermemory**: [repo](https://github.com/supermemoryai/supermemory) is MIT; the server ships as binaries only (v0.0.8, 2026-08-17), engine source not found.
  - V: 97% "Recall@20" ([research](https://supermemory.ai/research), 2026-05).
  - Adapter: one container per question, customId = session.
- **Letta**: the [server](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta) is retired (last release 0.16.8, 2026-05-14). Code now lives in [letta-code](https://github.com/letta-ai/letta-code) (Apache-2.0, v0.33.1, 2026-09-24), a separate agent defaulting to Letta Cloud.
  - LoCoMo 74.0% with gpt-4o-mini, V ([blog](https://www.letta.com/blog/benchmarking-ai-agent-memory/), 2025-08). LongMemEval: not found.
  - Adapter: one conversation per session, then message search.
- **Cognee**: [repo](https://github.com/topoteretes/cognee), Apache-2.0, v1.6.1 (2026-09-24).
  - BEAM-10M 0.67, V ([guide](https://www.cognee.ai/ai-memory-benchmarks), 2026-09). LongMemEval: not found.
  - Adapter: one document per session; rank by chunk hits.
- **Basic Memory**: [repo](https://github.com/basicmachines-co/basic-memory), AGPL-3.0, v0.23.2 (2026-08-25).
  - LoCoMo R@5 76.4%, V ([page](https://basicmemory.com/compare/mem0), 2026-06). LongMemEval: not found.
  - Adapter: one note per session.
- **OpenViking**: [repo](https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking), AGPL-3.0, v0.4.21 (2026-09-20).
  - LoCoMo 80–83% with Doubao models, V (README, v0.3.22). LongMemEval: not found.
  - Adapter: sessions as resources; map `find` URIs to sessions.
- **claude-mem**: [repo](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem), Apache-2.0, v13.25.3 (2026-09-21).
  - Benchmarks: not found.
  - Adapter: replay sessions as observations.
- **MemOS**: [repo](https://github.com/MemTensor/MemOS), Apache-2.0, v2.0.34 (2026-09-23).
  - V: LongMemEval 89.20 (2026-07, models unstated).
  - Needs Neo4j and Qdrant; its local plugin skips Claude Code and Codex.
  - Adapter: add sessions with a session ID.

## Risks

- **Comparability**:
  - agentmemory ([repo](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory), Apache-2.0, v0.9.29, 2026-08-16) publishes [95.2% recall_any](https://github.com/rohitg00/agentmemory/blob/main/benchmark/LONGMEMEVAL.md) but scored 0.821 recall_all in your harness.
  - Maximem found Mem0's QA prompts tuned to the benchmark.
  - MemPalace hybrid v4 was tuned on LongMemEval; report held-out only.
- **Realism**: 50-session haystacks are easy; pooling all 19,195 sessions dropped BM25 R@5 to 30% (#214). Add a pooled-store run.
- **Cost**: 470 questions mean about 22,100 session ingests, about 86 hours at Hindsight's measured gpt-oss-20b rate ([0.071/s](https://github.com/vectorize-io/hindsight-benchmarks/blob/main/results/leaderboard/llm/gcp-gpt-oss-20b-medium.json)). Subsample 100 questions; use one local model everywhere.
- **Licence and cloud**: Honcho, Basic Memory and OpenViking are AGPL. Supermemory's engine source was not found. Mem0 and Honcho default to cloud services.
- **Fit**: LongMemEval-S tests chat recall; [LongMemEval-V2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12493) (2026-05) tests agent trajectories.
